--- title: "Single-digit addition" subtitle: "Automatically generated task sheet · MATE_ARITMETIC_SUMA_1_DIGITO" --- ::: {.callout-note appearance="minimal"} **Automatically generated task sheet** (A · Accuracy; quality class B). Generated on November 28, 2026 with `scripts/R/ficha_generica_v3.R --tarea MATE_ARITMETIC_SUMA_1_DIGITO`. Figures come from the data; the theoretical framework is shared by the tasks of the same construct. **Interpretation and team review are missing.** Spanish name: *Sumas de un dígito*. [Spanish version](https://abarejo.github.io/leeduca-manual/fichas/auto/MATE_ARITMETIC_SUMA_1_DIGITO.html). ::: ::: {.callout-warning appearance="simple"} **Class B.** It has enough data to be described, but it lacks some of the guarantees of class A (stability across time points, item-level reliability or validity). Use with caution and not for individual decisions. [What each class means](../../limites.en.qmd#sec-clases). ::: **In one sentence.** Single-digit addition, from age 6 to 7 (2,452 administrations in 4 cohorts). AUC .74 against persistent reading difficulty. ## Description | | | |---|---| | Codes | 10759 2005 | | Battery | LEEDUCA | | Format | pictures on screen | | Items | 40 (10759); 37 (2005) according to the platform | | Task family | A · Accuracy | | Score | Correct responses | | Instructions (platform) | For 30 ss, the child makes one digit sums. | ## How it is programmed on the platform The platform is the reference: what the activity actually presents is what is measured. Configuration read from the activity itself on 28/10/2026 (without modifying it). Cell contents are in Spanish. | Code|Name on the platform |Presentation | Test items| Practice items|Example items |Time limit |Order |Scoring |Age.term (label 3) | |-----:|:--------------------|:---------------------------------------------|----------:|--------------:|:-------------|:----------|:-----|:----------|:------------------| | 10759|Sumas |Estímulo y opciones en pantalla; autoaplicada | 40| 0|— |60 s |fijo |Eficiencia |6, 6.2, 7.2 | | 2005|Suma - 1 Dígito |Estímulo y opciones en pantalla | 37| 0|— |30 s |fijo |Eficiencia |— | **Differences from the dictionary or the instructions (in Spanish):** - **10759.** 40 sumas con resultado (verificar), 60 s; autoaplicada. - **2005.** 37 sumas de un dígito; límite de 30 s. *Age.term: provisional reading of the activity's label 3 (3rd digit = age, 4th = term; 0 = annual), to be confirmed with the engineer.* **How it looks on the platform** (first item or example; 2026 screenshot; the interface is in Spanish). ::: {layout-ncol=2} ![10759 · Sumas](../../figuras/plataforma/10759.jpg){.lightbox fig-alt="Screenshot of activity 10759"} ![2005 · Suma - 1 Dígito](../../figuras/plataforma/2005.jpg){.lightbox fig-alt="Screenshot of activity 2005"} ::: ## Theoretical framework These tasks measure **arithmetic fluency**: solving simple additions and subtractions quickly, above all by retrieving arithmetic facts from memory. There are two formats. In the **production** formats (ages 6–8), the child says the result aloud and the examiner records it. In the **verification** formats (codes 107xx, school year 2021/22), the child sees the operation with a result and decides whether it is correct; they are self-administered and time-limited (60 or 120 s). **What the evidence says:** - **Producing and verifying are not exactly the same.** Production and verification errors are primed separately: verification relies more on the familiarity of the presented result [@campbell1996retrieval]. Scores from the two formats are not interchangeable. - **Arithmetic and reading fluency share predictors.** In 200 Finnish children followed from age 5 to 10, counting and RAN predicted both calculation and reading fluency [@koponen2013counting]. A common factor of RAN and verbal counting was the best predictor of what the two fluencies share [@koponen2020serial]. - **Phonological awareness is associated with fact retrieval, not with procedural calculation.** In 63 children with learning difficulties, phonemic awareness was related to problems solved from memory and not to those that require counting [@matejko2022phonological]. - **Difficulties are persistent and can be anticipated in preschool.** In 2,518 Finnish children followed from Grade 1 to Grade 9, 12% had persistent arithmetic fluency difficulties; preschool counting, number concepts and RAN distinguished this profile [@psyridou2023profiles]. **What our data show.** - **Production.** One-digit additions and two-digit additions and subtractions have acceptable consistency (α = .72–.76). They predict low arithmetic at ages 10–11 (AUC .59–.71) and, to the same extent, low Woodcock-Muñoz fluency (AUC .67–.74). The two-digit version has a ceiling at age 7 (23–33% maximum scores) and its screen shows a result, although the instructions ask the child to solve: which format was administered needs to be confirmed. - **Verification.** We do not yet have α for these versions. Their relation with concurrent low reading fluency is moderate (AUC .58–.69). The task for ages 10–11 (code 10748) is itself the low-arithmetic criterion ([Numerical cognition](../../cognicion-numerica.en.qmd#sec-mate-criterio)) and cannot be validated against it. - **Comorbidity.** Of 799 children aged 10–11, 19 have both low arithmetic and low reading, compared with 12.3 expected by chance. Together with the above, this supports a shared retrieval fluency. ## Sample and descriptive statistics | Time point| Cohort| Session|School year | N| Non-Preleo| Preleo| Schools| |----------:|------:|-------:|:-----------|---:|----------:|------:|-------:| | 6.2| 2010| 155|2016/17 | 915| 265| 650| 34| | 6.2| 2013| 903|2019/20 | 599| 382| 217| 31| | 6.3| 2011| 193|2017/18 | 679| 0| 679| 30| | 7.1| 2014| 950|2021/22 | 259| 0| 0| 8| | Time point| N| Cohorts| Mean| SD| Median| Skewness| % floor| % ceiling| |----------:|---:|----------:|----:|----:|------:|--------:|-------:|---------:| | 6.2| 647| 2010, 2013| 8.05| 3.12| 8| -0.08| 1.55| 0| **Score range** (non-Preleo group, in correct responses). The usual range goes from P1 to P99 (98% of the children). The minimum–maximum is the one observed after cleaning; the possible range is 0–37 correct responses. | Time point| N|Usual range (P1–P99) |Min.–max. |Possible range | Warning| |----------:|---:|:--------------------|:---------|:--------------|-------:| | 6.2| 647|0–15 |0–19 |0–37 | | ## Reliability There are no two time points with the same children (at least 80). α (2021) = .72. ## Validity **Concurrent.** Outside its domain, the highest relation is with: Word and text reading (6.2, r = .50); Word and text reading (6.3, r = .53); Reading comprehension (7.1, r = .22). **Against reading difficulty and comprehension.** Against persistent difficulty, AUC .74. Against poor comprehension one or two school years later (non-circular criterion), AUC .57–.65. ![Validity: AUC with 95% confidence interval (labels in Spanish).](../../figuras/Ficha_auto_MATE_ARITMETIC_SUMA_1_DIGITO_F2_validez.png){width=85%} **Against an external criterion, years later.** Against low Woodcock-Muñoz reading fluency in 2021/22 ([chapter](https://abarejo.github.io/leeduca-manual/criterio-woodcock.html), *in Spanish*), AUC .70–.73 (2 time points; 223–465 children). Against low arithmetic at ages 10–11 ([provisional criterion](https://abarejo.github.io/leeduca-manual/cognicion-numerica.html#sec-mate-criterio), *in Spanish*), AUC .69–.71. ## Provisional norms | Time point| N| Cohorts| P5| P10| P16| P25| P50| P75| P90| |----------:|---:|----------:|--:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | 6.2| 647| 2010, 2013| 3| 4| 5| 6| 8| 10| 12| | 6.3| 679| 2011| 4| 5| 7| 7| 9| 11| 13| | 7.1| 259| 2014| 4| 6| 8| 10| 14| 17| 19| These are norms by time point (school year × term). For dates between assessments and time points without a normative sample, study M3 proposes continuous norms on **months of instruction**, not on age, with relative age within the school year as an adjustment. ![Provisional norms (non-Preleo schools; labels in Spanish).](../../figuras/Ficha_auto_MATE_ARITMETIC_SUMA_1_DIGITO_F1_baremo.png){width=85%} ## Variables that affect it |Variable | Time point| n| Effect| p| |:---------------------------------------|----------:|-----:|------:|-----:| |School SES (ρ) | 6.2| 1,514| 0.147| 0.000| |Sex (d girl − boy; coding under review) | 6.2| 1,510| -0.276| 0.000| |Relative age (ρ with age in months) | 6.2| 1,511| 0.050| 0.053| |School (ICC) | 6.2| 1,514| 0.125| | |School SES (ρ) | 6.3| 679| 0.082| 0.032| |Sex (d girl − boy; coding under review) | 6.3| 678| -0.307| 0.000| |Relative age (ρ with age in months) | 6.3| 675| 0.144| 0.000| |School (ICC) | 6.3| 679| 0.063| | |Sex (d girl − boy; coding under review) | 7.1| 256| -0.301| 0.016| |Relative age (ρ with age in months) | 7.1| 256| 0.002| 0.968| |School (ICC) | 7.1| 259| 0.025| | ## For publications The LEEDUCA platform task “Single-digit addition” (codes 10759 and 2005; LEEDUCA battery) assesses arithmetic. The examiner presents each item orally, supported by a picture on the screen, and records the child's oral response. It comprises 37 items. The time limit is 120 seconds. It is administered individually on a computer at school. In the 2010, 2011, 2013 and 2014 cohorts it was administered in 4 sessions, from 6 to 7 years of age. The main outcome is the number of correct responses. In our data (2021 analyses), internal consistency was α = .72 (N = 2,337, 37 items). Against later poor reading comprehension, AUC = .57–.65. ## Pending issues - The task has several codes (versions or forms): check that time points are comparable before pooling norms. - Write the interpretation; review with the team.
